Studio now tells a call from the request it sent, says why a request got no answer and why a stream cannot connect, and keeps the credentials in error texts off everything that leaves its page. Its Playground reaches a proxy that admits browsers only, and the app's own address is learned from its server, never from a request. Nothing in your code changes — update every `@noverax` package together.

### Update every package together

- **Install 0.3.1 of every `@noverax` package at once.** An adapter from 0.3.0 beside a 0.3.1 core still tells the app's origin as its request's `Host` named it: only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` are taken from it, with one warning to update. A 0.3.1 runtime tells Studio how each stream's connection stands, which an older Studio does not know, and notes in its log as a rejected event.

### Security

- **The app's origin is learned from its server, never from a request.** Studio's Playground sends a Proxy-mode call — its headers and the `Authorization` you typed among them — to the app's own origin. In 0.3.0 that origin was learned from the first request's `Host`, so a request with a chosen `Host`, or a page whose name pointed at your machine, could send those calls to another host. Each adapter now tells the address its server listens on: the socket a request arrived on, the address `next dev` records as it starts, the one Studio's Vite plugin or Nuxt module sees the dev server listen on. Express, Fastify, NestJS, Hono and SolidStart learn it from the first request a Courier route serves; Next.js, SvelteKit, Astro, React Router and Nuxt before any request. See [How the app learns its origin](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/api/config#app-origin).
- **A stream the proxy relays keeps to its upstream's origin.** Its upstream connection followed any redirect with the source's headers, and handed another host's events on to the page. It now follows a redirect only on the upstream's own origin, as a proxied call does; a redirect elsewhere refuses the stream with `4000` plus the status, and a source that names its own `redirect` keeps it.
- **A Playground call keeps to the route's origin.** It followed any redirect the route, or a middleware in front of it, answered with, and took its headers along. It now follows a redirect only on the route's own origin, and says why it stopped at one it did not follow: the route's own, or the API's, which the proxy answers with its status alone.
- **Error texts lose their credentials as they leave Studio's page.** Studio wrote a failure's text as the app was told it — into `.courier/studio.db`, saved sessions and their exports, and what an agent is told. The page opened from Studio's link still shows each text whole; everything that leaves it has the credentials in its texts cut: an address's user, password and secret parameters, a header value the platform quoted, a JWT or a provider's key, a credential after `Bearer` or `Basic`, the value of a pair named as a secret. Your app cuts nothing and ships no code for it. See [Studio](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/studio/overview#start-studio).
- **Studio's code generator escapes what would end a script.** A value a specification gives is written with `<` and the two line separators escaped, so a generated literal stays whole wherever the code is put.

### Studio

- **A call is told apart from the request it sent.** Two identical reads made together send one request, and the second call waits for the first's answer. Studio's network figures — latency, throughput, bytes and error rates, the Audit's findings on size and caching, a session's figures, its HAR and Postman exports — now count requests; the Timeline's rows, the Middleware page and an agent's list count every call, and where the two differ both are shown: `14 calls · 5 requests`. A call another call's request answered is marked `shared`, its Timing tab says whose request it waited for, and a failed or slow request is toasted once, however many calls it answered. The request belongs to the first call still waiting when its answer comes: a call that left is never shared. See [Audit](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/studio/audit).
- **A request that got no answer says why.** Its Error tab names the system's code — `ENOTFOUND`, `ECONNREFUSED`, a certificate's, Bun's own — once, with the platform's text under the message; its Response tab, and the Playground's, say there was no answer instead of an empty body; and the suggested fix follows the code: a host name that did not resolve, a connection that failed, a certificate not trusted, an answer that broke as it arrived, an API that sent no headers in time, redirects with no end. A request a middleware failed because a connection of its own was refused says why too.
- **A stream that cannot connect says so.** It stood open and live while its client reconnected without a word. Its Messages tab and its Overview now say it is reconnecting, why its last connection ended, how many connections in a row failed and when the next one opens; the lists say *retrying*, and one that gives up before any connection opened says so, with the code and the fix. A stream the proxy relays tells how its upstream connection stands, and an ended stream says who closed it — its server, its caller, its lifetime, a server that shut down — where Studio said the server had completed every one.
- **The Playground reaches a proxy with `browsersOnly`.** A Proxy-mode call runs from your server's process, which sends no browser's headers, so `browsersOnly` refused every one with `403`. In development Studio's runtime now gives each call a one-time pass the proxy redeems: only `browsersOnly` is passed over, every other check applies, and no pass is honoured in production. Where the route cannot redeem it — an Edge route, a worker, a remote `appOrigin`, a runtime whose request headers cannot change — the Playground says why and offers to run the call in Direct mode. See [Proxy Mode](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/proxy-mode/overview).
- **A failure counts the same on every screen.** An answer its schema refused counts as failed on the status bar and Welcome, as it does in Analytics, the Explorer and the Audit.
- **A cancelled call is no failure.** A read a component cancelled as it went away, or a newer read took the place of, no longer toasts *Request failed*.
- **Settings → Recording names its limit Max calls**, since every call is a row of its own.
- The Courier mark keeps an icon's clear room in the Copy as menu and a request's snippets.

### Streams

- **A stream a Courier server serves opens at once.** It wrote nothing before its first event or its first heartbeat 25 s in, and a client heard it open only then; it now writes a comment as it opens, which every client passes over.
- **A stream refused with a redirect it does not follow ends**, with `4000` plus the status, as one refused with a 4xx does, rather than asking again on every reconnection. A 408, a 429 and a 5xx are retried as a dropped connection is. See [Realtime](https://courier.noverax.cloud/docs/advanced/realtime).

### Editors and agents

- **The VS Code extension's hints show the requests beside the calls**, where reads another call's request answered sent none, and the streams reconnecting apart from the ones open.
- **An agent is told calls and requests apart**, and every error text it reads with its credentials cut.

### create-courier

- **A project set up already is offered only what it lacks**, with what holds there said and nothing more; a part counts as done only where the app loads it.
- **It reads more of a project as it is**: its path aliases, a CommonJS config, a config under any name Studio reads, the files React Router, Remix, a Cloudflare worker and Fastify's autoload start from, JSX pages that hold closing tags or prose, the modules a file loads past a comment, and every star of an import's target.
- **It changes a project with care**: `package.json` keeps its layout, a peer or optional package counts only once it is installed, no name is bound twice, routes are mounted under a name left free, React Router's routes list none twice, no config is imported from outside a `rootDir`, a Next.js config that loads Studio is given its whole function, and the `routes` script is added only where a routes module or an `.expose(` is.
- **Hono is told apart in dev dependencies**, alone or beside the mock's.

All twenty packages move to 0.3.1.
